ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the direction of ray $OA$ is $15^\circ$ east of north, and the direction of ray $OB$ is $40^\circ$ west of north. Ray $OA$ is the angle bisector of $\angle BOC$. $OF$ is the extension line in the opposite direction of $OB$. Find: the direction of ray $OC$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} From the diagram, it is known that: $\angle AOB=15^\circ+40^\circ=55^\circ$,\\
since $OA$ is the angle bisector of $\angle BOC$,\\
thus $\angle AOC=55^\circ$,\\
therefore $\angle NOC=\angle NOA+\angle AOC$\\
$=15^\circ+55^\circ=70^\circ$,\\
hence, the ray $OC$ is in the direction of \boxed{70^\circ} East of North.

Read from the text that OA is 15° east of north, OB is 40° west of north, and OA bisects ∠BOC. Compute the smaller angle ∠BOA as 40° + 15° = 55° because OB and OA lie on opposite sides of the north line. Since OA is the angle bisector, ∠AOC must also be 55°. Starting from north to OA is 15°, then continue another 55° toward OC, giving ∠NOC = 70°. Therefore OC is 70° east of north.
